newsitem.title: FRANCE: Law courts bombed in French city of Aix.
newsitem.headline: Law courts bombed in French city of Aix.

text.p: A bomb exploded in front of the law courts in the southern city of Aix-en-Provence early on Sunday, damaging the facade and a ground-floor administrative office, police said. There were no casualties.
No one immediately claimed responsibility for the blast, but the same building was badly damaged in a November 1992 blast claimed by Corsican separatists.
Militant nationalists on the French Mediterranean island of Corsica have been waging a low-level guerrilla war for the past two decades in search of greater autonomy from mainland France.
One separatist group had recently threatened to carry its struggle to the mainland.

In the Corsican city of Ajaccio, meanwhile, police said that two separatists, suspected in a series of post office bombings, had been transferred to Paris on Sunday morning , where they would be taken before an anti-terrorist judge.
The suspects had been arrested in Corsica on Thursday in connection with the bombings which took place last weekend.
French Prime Minister Alain Juppe has decreed a crackdown on separatist violence, but nationalist leaders have in turn accused him of burying secret talks aimed at resolving their differences.
